## Summary

I implemented the 0/1 knapsack solution so all tests pass.

**`knapsack.h`** — added the function declaration and a `<vector>` include:
```cpp
int maximum_value(int max_weight, const std::vector<Item>& items);
```

**`knapsack.cpp`** — implemented `maximum_value` using a 1-D dynamic-programming table of size `max_weight + 1`. For each item it iterates capacity in **descending** order (`max_weight` down to `item.weight`) so each item is used at most once, updating:
```cpp
dp[weight] = std::max(dp[weight], dp[weight - item.weight] + item.value);
```
It returns `dp[max_weight]`. This is O(n · max_weight) time and O(max_weight) space.
